name: Outbound LinkedIn DM Rubric (Hard Mode)
description: Score an outbound LinkedIn DM. Designed to heavily penalize messages that ignore fundamental qualification mismatches. Max score ~30 before penalties. Most messages should score 10-18.

sections.title: Qualification & Fit Assessment
criteria: +4 explicitly acknowledges how candidate's background maps to role requirements
+3 identifies SPECIFIC transferable skills (not just 'your experience is relevant')
+3 addresses obvious gaps or mismatches honestly (if any exist)
penalties: -8 ignores fundamental qualification mismatch (e.g., role requires PhD but candidate has BS)
-6 ignores domain mismatch (e.g., ML engineer for Finance Tutor role requiring CFA)
-5 ignores location/visa requirements when role is onsite-only
-4 ignores seniority mismatch (pitching IC role to VP, or senior role to 2-year candidate)

sections.title: Genuine Personalization
criteria: +4 references a SPECIFIC achievement with concrete detail (metric, outcome, company)
+2 draws a non-obvious connection between candidate's work and role
+2 shows evidence of reading the profile (not just keyword extraction)
penalties: -6 generic phrases that could apply to anyone ('your impressive background')
-4 copy-pastes text from the candidate profile without adding insight
-3 mentions skills without explaining why they matter for THIS role
-2 uses name but nothing else specific

sections.title: Value Proposition
criteria: +3 explains what makes THIS role uniquely interesting (not generic 'great company')
+1 mentions specific opportunities (growth, impact, technical challenge)
penalties: -2 value prop could apply to any company/role

sections.title: Call to Action
penalties: -2 no clear CTA or multiple conflicting asks

global_penalties: -10 hallucinated facts about candidate (wrong company, fake project, wrong name)
-8 hallucinated facts about role (wrong title, made-up requirements)
-6 message ignores that candidate likely doesn't meet core requirements
-4 message is clearly a template with blanks filled in
-3 over 150 words (LinkedIn DMs should be scannable)
-2 under 40 words (too brief to be compelling)

calibration_examples.scenario: Finance Tutor role (requires PhD Economics) sent to ML Engineer with MS CS
calibration_examples.bad_message: Hi! Your experience with PyTorch and distributed systems is impressive. We're hiring Finance Tutors at xAI!
calibration_examples.why_bad: Completely ignores that candidate has zero finance/economics background and the role requires a PhD in Economics. Score: 2-5
calibration_examples.good_message: Hi - I know this is unconventional, but xAI's Finance Tutor role involves teaching AI models, not traditional tutoring. Your ML background could bring a unique perspective to how we structure financial reasoning problems. Would you be open to a quick chat about whether this could be interesting?
calibration_examples.why_good: Acknowledges the mismatch, explains why it might still work, gives candidate context. Score: 18-22

calibration_examples.scenario: Senior SRE role (5+ years required) sent to 2-year junior engineer
calibration_examples.bad_message: Your infrastructure experience is exactly what we need for our Senior SRE role!
calibration_examples.why_bad: Ignores that candidate has 2 years experience vs 5+ required. Score: 3-6
calibration_examples.good_message: Hi - I noticed you've done impressive work on Kubernetes in your 2 years at Datadog. Our Senior SRE role typically needs 5+ years, but we sometimes make exceptions for strong candidates. Would you be interested in a conversation about the role and whether the fit could work?
calibration_examples.why_good: Honest about the gap, explains why reaching out anyway. Score: 16-20

scoring_guidance.25-30: Exceptional. Handles any mismatches elegantly, genuinely personalized, compelling value prop. VERY RARE.
scoring_guidance.18-24: Good. Acknowledges candidate's actual background, addresses fit thoughtfully, specific details.
scoring_guidance.12-17: Mediocre. Some personalization but misses key fit issues or uses generic language.
scoring_guidance.6-11: Poor. Template-like, ignores obvious qualification gaps, generic phrases.
scoring_guidance.0-5: Spam. Could be sent to anyone, ignores everything about the candidate's actual background.
